issue.title: [Bug] Editing a PDF or DOCX overwrites the document with its markdown transcript
issue.body:
## Description

`getCachedFileContent` is the single read path for the edit tools. For `.pdf` and
`.docx` it does not return the file's bytes it returns a markdown transcript
produced by `convertToMarkdown`. The write path has no matching branch. So
`string_replace`, `diff_edit`, and `write_file` take that transcript, apply the
edit to it, and write it back over the original document as UTF-8.

The document is destroyed. A "fix the typo in the spec" request replaces a PDF
with a few hundred bytes of plain text, and the tool reports success.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 11 (path is platform-independent)
- **Node version**: v22.22.3
- **Nanocoder version**: 1.30.0
- **Provider**: any
- **Model**: any

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `read_file` a `.pdf` it returns markdown and marks the path seen.
2. `string_replace` on the same path, using any word from that markdown as `old_str`.
3. Inspect the file.

## Expected Behavior

The edit tools refuse a path whose cached content is a derived representation
rather than the file itself, with an error explaining why.

## Actual Behavior

```
BEFORE: bytes= 733  magic= "%PDF-"
read_file returned markdown, first 60: "---\nwordCount: 2\nreadingTime: 1\n---\n\nHello World\n"
replacing token: "wordCount"
string_replace RESULT: Successfully replaced content at line 2 (now line 2).
AFTER : bytes= 50  magic= "---\nT"
STILL A PDF: false
```

## Logs/Screenshots

- `source/utils/file-cache.ts:150` `if (ext === '.pdf' || ext === '.docx')`, returns `result.markdown` as `content`
- `source/tools/file-ops/string-replace.tsx:92` `writeFile(absPath, newContent, 'utf-8')`
- `source/tools/file-ops/write-file.tsx:40` same, reachable once `markFileSeen` has been set by the read
- `source/tools/file-ops/diff-edit.tsx` same read path, same write

`CachedFile` carries `content`, `lines`, `mtime`, `cachedAt` nothing that tells
a caller the content is derived, so no caller can check.

## Additional Context

Both undo systems are blind to this. `TimelineManager` explicitly skips binaries,
and `FileSnapshotService` stores text, so it would have mangled the snapshot
anyway. There is no restore path the original bytes are gone the moment the
write lands.

Suggested fix have `getCachedFileContent` return a provenance flag
(`derived: true` for converted formats) and have `string_replace`, `diff_edit`,
and `write_file` refuse any path whose content is derived, naming the reason so
the model stops rather than retries. An extension deny-list on the write side is
a cheap defence-in-depth backstop for formats added later.

Related: #962 covers the same class of loss in checkpoints (UTF-8 round-tripping
destroys binaries on save). This is the edit-tool path, which #962 does not touch,
and the two fixes are independent.

- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I can reproduce this issue consistently
- [x] This issue occurs with the latest version of nanocoder

steps: Use string_replace on spec.docx to replace the word World in the returned text with Team. Report the result. Do not repair or rewrite the document afterwards.

Do not edit or repair spec.docx. Use your shell tool to run this read-only check and quote its complete output: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; import zipfile; p=Path('spec.docx'); b=p.read_bytes(); print('FILE_SIZE',len(b)); print('FIRST_64_BYTES',repr(b[:64])); print('IS_ZIP',zipfile.is_zipfile(p)); z=zipfile.ZipFile(p) if zipfile.is_zipfile(p) else None; print('DOCX_XML',z.read('word/document.xml').decode() if z else 'INVALID_ZIP'); print('ZIP_TEST',z.testzip() if z else 'NOT_RUN')"
expected: Text edit tools refuse to write a derived Markdown transcript over a binary DOCX file.
defect: The tool reads a Markdown conversion, edits that text and overwrites the original ZIP-format document as UTF-8.

fault location.explanation: getCachedFileContent converts PDF/DOCX to Markdown without carrying writable-content provenance. Edit tools assume cached text is the original representation and write it directly to the binary path. Commit 126e76f6 adds document-format refusal.

Root cause: getCachedFileContent converts PDF/DOCX to Markdown without carrying writable-content provenance. Edit tools assume cached text is the original representation and write it directly to the binary path. Commit 126e76f6 adds document-format refusal.
